source.title: Impact of Data Duplication on Deep Neural Network-Based Image Classifiers: Robust vs. Standard Models
source.authors: Alireza Aghabagherloo; Aydin Abadi; Sumanta Sarkar; Vishnu Asutosh Dasu; Bart Preneel

record.tranche_reason: Tests how a different training-data intervention—adding duplicates—affects generalization on Gaussian data and CIFAR-10; it does not test the listed claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports generalization and accuracy outcomes under duplicated-data conditions. These findings concern the claim's subject but none measures a behavior named by V1–V8. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests training-data duplication, which none of V1–V8 names. It does not measure random-label fitting, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or removal of examples selected by memorization influence. Its citation of Feldman and Zhang does not constitute a test of V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: duplication can sometimes help but does not consistently improve generalization, can harm accuracy under non-uniform duplication or adversarial training, and increases training work. The standard CIFAR-10 experiment shows modest gains with diminishing returns.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies training-set duplication; the claim versions concern memorization, architecture, optimizers, batch size, regularization, sharpness, and memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects differ between standard and adversarially trained CIFAR-10 models and between uniform and non-uniform duplication; the text also reports outcomes at different duplication rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-uniform duplication at D-rate 40 reduced Gaussian SVM overall accuracy from 0.76 to 0.72.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-biased duplication can shift class-specific accuracy and lower overall classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard CIFAR-10 test accuracy increased from 70.72% without duplication to 74.12% at 30% duplication and 75.11% at 60%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniformly sampled training duplicates can improve standard CIFAR-10 accuracy, with diminishing gains as duplication increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarially trained CIFAR-10 clean-test accuracy decreased from 41.16% without duplication to 27.39% at 30% duplication and 20.90% at 60%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniformly sampled training duplicates can reduce clean-test accuracy in adversarially trained image classifiers.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 experiments are described as a toy example; model architecture and size, most training details, uncertainty estimates, and numerical adversarial-accuracy results are not stated in the supplied text. Some outcomes are shown in figures without a full numerical series in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from Figure 1 or Figure 2 were extracted where the text gives only figure-based trends or lacks separately stated numerical values. The reported Gaussian examples and CIFAR-10 results are included above.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy compared with natural-label generalization using the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contributions of local connectivity and initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects, including small-data regimes, excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Adding duplicate examples does not test removing examples selected by memorization influence. The discussion of prior memorization research supplies no new V8 result. Additional duplication trends are already declared in rows_left_out and do not bear on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Network-width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: SVM with RBF kernel
rows.operation_detail: Train on the original Gaussian dataset without duplicates.
rows.note: Reported as the original overall accuracy for the D-rate = 40 comparison; the result does not measure any listed version.
rows.check: The reported 0.76 baseline is correct; Gaussian SVM accuracy does not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: SVM with RBF kernel
rows.operation_detail: Add duplicates with selection probabilities 0.7 for label 1 and 0.3 for label −1.
rows.note: The study describes a decrease in overall accuracy after non-uniform duplication.
rows.check: Change partial to cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. The decrease from 0.76 to 0.72 under non-uniform duplication is correctly recorded but measures a different intervention.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 standard model

rows.note: Baseline for the standard-model duplication comparison.
rows.check: The 70.72% baseline is correct; natural-label test accuracy alone does not establish V1.
